issues.should_be: damage_photos.zip was attached to the email and is counted as received (photos OK). But repair_quote.pdf is NOT a document belonging to this policyholder and vehicle: it names customer 'Mr. Julien Roche', vehicle 'Renault Clio (2017)', registration 'DX-482-KD', whereas the Policy Schedule holder is Ines Haddad with a Toyota Yaris (2019). The required C2 repair quote for the insured vehicle is therefore not validly provided. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>
issues.evidence: repair_quote.pdf header: 'Customer Mr. Julien Roche... Vehicle Renault Clio (2017), Registration: DX-482-KD' vs Policy Schedule: holder_name 'Ines Haddad', vehicle 'Toyota Yaris (2019)'; contract Article 4.3 requires for C2 'Photos of the damage; repair quote' <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>.

Deadline OK: reported 2026-10-29, within 5 days of the 2026-10-28 incident (Article 4.1 <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>). No exclusion signal (Article 3). Coverage C2 is in the Policy Schedule (Article 2). Assessor not required: repair cost €980 is not above €1,500 (Article 6.1 <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>). Playbook commercial-vehicle referral rule does not apply: email states no one else was involved, so no commercial third-party vehicle. BUT the staged payment rests on repair_quote.pdf, which belongs to a different customer and vehicle (Mr. Julien Roche, Renault Clio 2017, DX-482-KD) — not policyholder Ines Haddad's Toyota Yaris (2019). The C2-required repair quote for the insured vehicle (Article 4.3) is therefore not validly provided; per Article 4.3 a missing document is requested from the policyholder rather than paid on. A quote for another person's car cannot support a €680 payout on VER-1003.
